messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "Our method achieves the highest SSIM and the lowest LMD, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of our method." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "From Table 2, we observe that our model achieves the highest SSIM and the lowest LMD, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of our method."
2. "Our method surpasses other methods on the metrics of both SSIM and LMD." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "Although the PSNR of our method is a little lower than that of Chen et al. [Chen et al. , 2019], our method surpass [Chen et al. , 2019] on the metrics of both SSIM and LMD."
3. "The quantitative results in Table 1 show that our method has the highest PSNR and SSIM, indicating its ability to generate high-quality videos." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "Table 1 shows the quantitative results of our method and its competitors with higher PSNR, SSIM and lower LMD, suggesting the best quality of the generated video frames of the talking faces."
4. "The generation examples in Figure 5 show that our method can generate more realistic and synchronous frames compared to Zhou et al. and Chen et al." -- cites: E5 (Figure 5): observation "The zoomed view of Figure 5 shows that our method can generate more realistic and synchronous frames compared to Zhou et al. and Chen et al."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section L, page 5): 4.2 Quantitative Results We compare our model with four recent state-of-the-art methods, including Chung et al. [2017], Chen et al. [2018] Zhou et al. [2019], and Chen et al. [2019]. Table 1 shows the quantitative results of our method and its competitors with higher PSNR, SSIM and lower LMD, suggesting the best quality of the generated video frames of the talking faces. Although Zhou et al. [Zhou et al. , 2019] obtains the lowest PSNR, it obtains the second highest SSIM and its SSIM is signiﬁcantly better than Chung et al. [Chung et al. , 2017] and Chen et al. [Chen et al. , 2018]. To further verify the robustness for arbitrary person generation, we evaluate our method on another benchmark dataset GRID [Cooke et al. , 2006] and report the comparison results in Table 2. From Table 2, we observe that our model achieves the highest SSIM and the lowest LMD, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of our method. Although the PSNR of our method is a little lower than that of Chen et al. [Chen et al. , 2019], our method surpass [Chen et al. , 2019] on the metrics of both SSIM and LMD. Therefore, our method always achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM, demonstrating our method is able to generate high-quality videos.
[E5] (figure, Figure 5, page 5) (image attached): Figure 5: Generation examples of our method comparing with Ground Truth (G.T.) (a), and Zhou et al. and Chen et al. (b). (Better zoom in to see the detail). [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E1 (Section L) states that the method achieves the highest SSIM and the lowest LMD, which directly supports the claim.
The evidence in E1 (Section L) mentions that the method surpasses other methods on the metrics of both SSIM and LMD, which supports the claim.

The evidence in E1 (Section L) states that the method has the highest PSNR and SSIM, but it does not explicitly state that the method has the highest PSNR and SSIM in Table 1. The claim is not fully supported by the evidence.
The evidence in E5 (Figure 5) shows that the method can generate more realistic and synchronous frames compared to Zhou et al. and Chen et al., which supports the claim.
